In Node.js a file is either an ES module or a CommonJS module. A file with an `import` declaration is an ES module, where `module` and `exports` do not exist, so `module.exports = ...` throws a `ReferenceError`. Bundlers and transpilers that accept the mix do not agree on what such a file exports.

The import declarations are what is reported. Any property of `module` counts, so `module.hot` in a file with imports is reported too.

The entry point of a package is exempt: the file that `main` in the closest `package.json` points to, or its `index.js`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
import { parse } from "./parse";

module.exports = { run: text => parse(text) };
```

{/* bad */}
```js
import { parse } from "./parse";

exports.run = text => parse(text);
```

{/* bad */}
```js
import { render } from "./render";

if (module.hot) {
  module.hot.accept(render);
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
import { parse } from "./parse";

export const run = text => parse(text);
```

{/* good */}
```js
const { parse } = require("./parse");

module.exports = { run: text => parse(text) };
```

The entry point:

{/* file "package.json" */}
```json package.json
{ "name": "runner", "main": "lib/runner.js" }
```

{/* good {"filename": "lib/runner.js"} */}
```js lib/runner.js
import { parse } from "./parse";

module.exports = { run: text => parse(text) };
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exceptions` | `[]` | Globs for files that are not checked. They are matched against the full path, so start them with `**/`. |

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"import/no-import-module-exports" = ["error", { exceptions = ["**/*.config.js"] }]
```
